text:
The Golden Knights are doing what they usually do in November: winning, and making it look routine. Vegas beat Utah 5-3 on Wednesday for a fourth straight win, outscoring opponents 14-7 in the run, and the chances back it this time (54% of the expected goals in those games). They are 13-5-2, with 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) on the season.

Nothing about this is luck-driven. The shooters are scoring almost exactly what their chances deserve, and the goaltending, split between Adin Hill and Carter Hart, is a couple of goals better than expected. The penalty kill is the piece that doesn't get headlines: 0.47 expected goals against a game. Victor Olofsson is the hot hand, with 9 points in 7 games on chances worth 4.2, and Mitch Marner had three assists against Utah.

The top line of Mark Stone, Ivan Barbashev and Jack Eichel has outscored opponents 10-4 with 59% of the chances, and Brayden McNabb and Shea Theodore have been dominant, 20-9 in more than 300 minutes. The soft spots are the Nic Dowd line (30% of the chances) and the Rasmus Andersson and Jeremy Lauzon pair (36%). Parker Wotherspoon's return from injured reserve gives the blue line another option there. Rookie Trevor Connelly, with a late winner in Detroit, has SinBin.vegas arguing for a bigger role.

Our numbers give Vegas a 98% chance at the playoffs, projecting about 106 points.
